newsitem.title: USA: News Corp to relaunch Web service.
newsitem.headline: News Corp to relaunch Web service.

text.p: After a turbulent first year on the Internet, Rupert Murdoch's News Corp will launch its revamped entertainment Web site on the Internet on Monday with a redirected strategy using the content and popular brand name of TV Guide, one the media giant's best-known brand names.

The TV Guide Entertainment Network will remain free on the Internet. News Corp expects money generated through advertising sales and eventual on-line transactions will allow it to turn a profit within three to five years.

"Three to five years is the timeframe," said James Murdoch, Rupert Murdoch's youngest son, who serves as vice president, music and new media of News Corp, when asked about profitability goals for the site.

The TV Guide Entertainment Network (www.tvguide.com), will have four areas, or channels, with listings and data about television, movies, music and sports. Fox Sports and other Murdoch properties will also provide content, News Corp said.

News Corp is also embracing the WebTV Internet access device. Through an agreement with WebTV Networks Inc in Palo Alto, Calif., it will develop customized television-oriented content for the WebTV, which turns a standard TV into an Internet access device.

Murdoch dismissed any suggestion that News Corp's foray on the Internet has so far been less than successful, even after the its partner MCI Communications Corp pulled out of their joint online venture, an Internet directory service called iGuide, last February.

"When something is at the very beginning in a new medium, it changes very quickly," Murdoch said. "Like everyone else in new media, we've been evolving... A year ago, we redirected it. It's been a well-kept secret on the Internet. Now it's a question of reaching users and telling them it's there."

Peter Krasilovksy, an analyst with Arlen Communications Inc in Bethesda, Md, said he believed "iGuide is one of the overlooked sites on the Web" but "It got lost in the corporate brouhaha between MCI and News Corp."
Murdoch pointed to data from market research firm PC Meter, which counts the current iGuide site (before revamp) as number 96 out of 3,000 Web sites surveyed, up from about 500th or so a year ago.
Pamela Smith, a vice president at PC Meter, said "They really have grown from a very low amount of traffic." She noted that "They were 96 in October. And it's a fairly new service."

News Corp hopes to gain repeat visitors who will check the site for TV listings. It can then build up demographic profiles to further enhance the site for advertisers, including localized advertising. TV listings can be localized by typing in a zip code.
With more than 200,000 pages of content, the TV Guide Entertainment Network will be able to offer and customize content with co-branded ad packages, it said.

A big auditorium chat with celebrities, specialized bulletin boards, big databases of entertainment facts and trivia, and games are a few of the features News Corp hopes will draw Internet users to the site.
So far, the site has had 10 million page views per month, Murdoch said, but the company hopes its revamped site will be an even greater success.
"We really think this year will be very good for us," Murdoch said.
